title: Scalable Microfabricated High Torque Mechanical Micromotors
text: A new excitation technique based on the rectification of the oscillatory motion was used in surface micromachined 2-5 µm- thick LPCVD polysilicon micromotors with large torques. The 160 µm - 1600 µm diameter rotors consisted of a pivoted circular disk with perimeter cantilevers that bend and generate a twisting force upon actuation by a vibrating stator. The vibrations can be generated and harvested by and from many different sources. Here comb drives were used for feasibility studies. In comparison to electrostatic side-drive micromotors, the torques were larger and the maximum torque of up to 46 nanoN-m was observed and measured. The micromotors generated these large torques with relatively thin (<5 µm) rotors, they are fully compatible with IC processing, they can be scaled over a large range of diameters while requiring nearly constant excitation voltages, and there are no voltages applied directly to their rotors.
